newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's BLOM buys French bank for $53 million.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's BLOM buys French bank for $53 million.

text.p: Lebanon's Banque du Liban et d'Outre Mer (BLOM) said on Thursday its purchase of Paris-based Banque Banorabe-France which has branches in London and the Gulf and a subsidiary in Switzerland cost an estimated $53 million.
BLOM announced on Wednesday that it had bought all shares in the Paris-based bank. It simultaneously announced that it doubled its own capital at end 1996 to over $150 million from $77 million.

The capital increase made BLOM one of the giants of Lebanese banking beside Banque de la Mediterranee, owned by billionaire Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri, which announced this week that it had increased its capital to $212 million from $102 million.
It said on Wednesday that acquisition of Banorabe made it "the Lebanese bank with the largest presence in major European and Arab financial centres."

Giving new details of its transactions in response to questions from Reuters, BLOM said in its latest statement that the increase in shareholders' equity was carried out by cash injection and accumulation of profits.
"The number of BLOM shareholders increased effectively from 245 to 296," the statement said.
On the bank purchase, it said: "Banorabe was acquired at a cost of $53 million as estimated by a leading international audit firm."

Banorabe-France was previously owned by Banorabe Holdings which was owned by the same shareholders as BLOM. The French bank has branches in London, Dubai, Sharjah and Muscat and owns Geneva-based Banque Banorient.
The purpose of the acquisition was to strengthen the ownership structure of the French and Swiss banks and establish a homogeneous banking group, BLOM's statement said.
However, the Banorabe group would remain legally and administratively independent under the supervision of the French authorities, it added.
The BLOM group's policy would remain "very cautious due to the situation in the Middle East," it said.

Asked whether BLOM would follow other leading Beirut banks in raising funds on the international market, the statement said: "At the present time BLOM would not raise funds on the international markets. The bank is very liquid and the loans are mainly of commercial short term nature."
It also said in reply to a question that it had no immediate plan to list its shares on the Beirut Stock Exchange but did not rule out this possibility at a later stage.
